function.name: ProductSearch_execute
function.description: Performs a search for products in the database based on specified criteria, such as keywords and filters, and returns a list of matching products. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

keywords.description: The search terms used to find products, separated by spaces.

category.description: The category to filter the search results. If no category is specified, all categories will be included in the search.

price_range.description: A price range to narrow down the search results, specified as a string in the format 'min-max' where min and max are prices in USD.

sort_order.description: The order in which the search results are sorted. Choose 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

in_stock.description: A flag to filter search results to only include products that are in stock. Set to true to include only in-stock items.

message.content:
It depends on a few things—your skin tone, the occasion, and the vibe you’re going for. Here’s a quick guide:

| Factor | Cream‑colored look works best if… | Cream might clash if… |
|--------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Skin tone** | Warm undertones (yellow, golden, olive) | Cool undertones (pink, rosy, blue) |
| **Hair color** | Light to medium brown, auburn, or blonde | Dark brown or black (unless you’re going for a dramatic contrast) |
| **Eye color** | Brown, hazel, or green | Blue or gray (they can look washed out against cream) |
| **Occasion** | Casual brunch, daytime events, relaxed office | Formal evening events, high‑contrast themes |
| **Style** | Soft, boho, vintage, or minimalist | Edgy, streetwear, or bold, neon palettes |

**Why it works:** Cream is a neutral that pairs well with most colors—especially muted pastels, earth tones, and even jewel tones for a subtle pop. It’s also flattering on warm skin tones because it echoes the natural warmth of your complexion.

**When to be cautious:** If you have a cool undertone, cream can sometimes make you look washed out. In that case, try off‑white, light gray, or a soft pastel instead.

**Quick test:** Hold a cream fabric (or a cream‑colored shirt) up to your face in natural light. If your skin looks luminous and the color doesn’t make you look sallow, go for it! If it feels too pale or you’re unsure, consider a slightly warmer or cooler shade.

Bottom line: If you’re comfortable and the setting is casual or daytime, cream is a safe, stylish choice—especially if you have warm undertones. If you’re aiming for a more formal or high‑contrast look, you might want to pick a different neutral or add a pop of color to keep things interesting.
